complexity_scope.guarantee: Worst-case expected lower bound, with an oblivious hard path chosen for each policy.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Universal c=1/(32sqrt(2)) supplied by the local argument; independent of K,T,V_T. No claim of the best constant.
complexity_scope.oracle: One selected-arm Bernoulli observation per round; all unselected rewards remain hidden.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: T online actions; expected cumulative dynamic pseudoregret against the per-round best mean, exactly the selected-means metric of P100 p.8.
complexity_scope.regime: K>=2,T>=2,1/K<=V_T<=T/K, including T<K and a nominal batch size exceeding T.
complexity_scope.resource: T arm pulls and T reward observations; no arithmetic, memory or runtime lower bound is asserted.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Every nonanticipating randomized policy with selected-arm feedback; unrestricted computation and no support or output constraint beyond online arm selection.

construction_notes.coverage_and_escape: Covers all selected-arm nonanticipating policies, with arbitrary internal computation. Multiple observations per round, full information, side information revealing J_j, anticipatory policies and different variation metrics are outside the established coverage.
construction_notes.hidden_objects: Independent uniform good-arm identity J_j per batch, chosen before interaction; all reward bits are hidden except the selected ones.
construction_notes.oracle_realization: Independent Bernoulli reward vectors conditional on the fixed path, with mean 1/2+eps for J_j and 1/2 otherwise; the full local argument conditions on seed and actual past before comparing current-batch laws.
construction_notes.public_information: K,T,V_T, the prior and batch boundaries may be known. The proof does not require secret boundaries.

proofs.full_local_argument:
LOCAL REPAIR, not a quotation or an independently reviewed proof. Write V=V_T, a=K^(1/3)(T/V)^(2/3), D=ceil(a), b=(KV/T)^(1/3), and eps=min{sqrt(K/D)/4,VD/T}. Since V<=T/K, a>=K>=2, a<=D<=2a, and 0<eps<=1/4. Partition {1,...,T} into m=ceil(T/D) batches of lengths n_j<=D, allowing D>T (then m=1). Draw J_1,...,J_m independently uniformly on {1,...,K}, before interaction, independently of the policy seed. In batch j set mu_t^k=1/2+eps*1{k=J_j}. Conditional on the entire J vector, generate mutually independent Bernoulli rewards of these means across arms and times, independently of the seed. This is a chosen admissible hard subclass, not an independence restriction on the policies or on the whole environment class. Every path has V(mu;T)<=(m-1)eps<=T eps/D<=V, even when D>T. The schedule, parameters and prior can be public.

Fix any measurable nonanticipating randomized policy. Represent all its internal randomness by its independent seed U. At a batch start fix U=u and a possible past observed reward history h; past actions are then determined. The new J_j is still uniform and independent of (u,h), since past observations involve only earlier batches. For each fixed u,h the within-batch policy is a deterministic function of the new binary observations and has no access to J_j. Compare length-n observation-string laws P_0 (all means 1/2 in this batch) and P_k (only arm k has mean 1/2+eps), with the same fixed u,h. All binary strings have positive probability. Let N_k be the selected-arm count, a function of that string, 0<=N_k<=n. This comparison keeps the past fixed; it does not replace the actual past by a baseline-generated past.

Using natural logarithms, let L=-ln(1-4eps^2). The log ratio of the two observation-string probabilities is the sum of their conditional log ratios, by multiplication of conditional probabilities. Taking expectation under P_0, a round with selected arm other than k contributes zero; a round selecting k contributes d(1/2||1/2+eps)=-(1/2)ln(1-4eps^2)=L/2. Hence D_KL(P_0||P_k)=(L/2)E_0 N_k. This identity holds for this deterministic continuation for every u,h; no reset of the policy is required.

For completeness the finite-distribution inequality used here is proved locally. For positive probability distributions P,Q, let A={r:P(r)>=Q(r)}, p=P(A), q=Q(A), and v=p-q=(1/2)sum_r|P(r)-Q(r)|. Grouping the relative entropy over A and its complement gives D_KL(P||Q)>=d(p||q). Indeed, in each group Jensen's inequality for the convex function x ln x with weights Q(r)/Q(group) gives sum_group P(r)ln(P(r)/Q(r))>=P(group)ln(P(group)/Q(group)); sum the two groups. For fixed q in (0,1), d(p||q) has value and first derivative zero at p=q and second derivative 1/[p(1-p)]>=4; integrating twice gives d(p||q)>=2(p-q)^2. Degenerate groups follow by continuity, or P=Q gives v=0. Thus v<=sqrt(D_KL(P||Q)/2). For 0<=f<=M, E_Q f-E_P f<=M sum_{Q>P}(Q-P)=Mv. Applying this with P=P_0,Q=P_k gives E_k f-E_0 f<=(M/2)sqrt(L E_0 N_k). This reproduces Auer Lemma A.1 with natural logarithms, without leaving a mathematical dependency unproved.

Apply the preceding inequality with f=N_k and M=n. Since sum_k E_0 N_k=n, Cauchy-Schwarz gives (1/K)sum_k E_k N_k <= n/K+(n/(2K))sqrt(LKn). Conditional expected dynamic pseudoregret in this batch, averaged over the fresh uniform J_j, is exactly eps[n-(1/K)sum_k E_k N_k], since mu_t^*-mu_t^{I_t}=eps*1{I_t!=J_j}. It is therefore at least eps*n[1-1/K-(1/2)sqrt(Ln/K)]. This is a statement about selected means directly; no equality with realized reward regret is assumed.

Set x=4eps^2<=1/4. Since -ln(1-x)=integral_0^x (1-s)^(-1) ds <= x/(1-x)<=4x/3, L<=16eps^2/3. As n<=D and eps<=sqrt(K/D)/4, (1/2)sqrt(Ln/K)<= (2eps/sqrt(3))*sqrt(D/K)<=1/(2sqrt(3)). Consequently the bracket is at least 1/2-1/(2sqrt(3))>1/8 for K>=2. This uniform conditional bound can be integrated over the actual u,h distribution at each batch start, including any dependence of the history on earlier J values. Summing n_j=T gives prior-averaged regret >=T eps/8 for every policy.

Finally sqrt(K/D)/4>=sqrt(K/(2a))/4=b/(4sqrt(2)), while VD/T>=Va/T=b. Thus eps>=b/(4sqrt(2)), and the prior-averaged regret is at least (KV)^(1/3)T^(2/3)/(32sqrt(2)). The prior has finitely many deterministic mean paths, each already shown admissible, so at least one such path has expected regret at least this average, after integrating all reward and policy randomness. Taking the supremum over paths and then the infimum over policies proves the assigned minimax rate, uniformly for all integer K>=2,T>=2 and V in [1/K,T/K], with c=1/(32sqrt(2)). No T>=K or D<=T condition was introduced. The source's final 1/(4sqrt(2)) coefficient is not used; the displayed constant here is a conservative local repair requiring new independent complete_local_argument_checked review.

assumptions: An oblivious mean-path adversary; at each round one arm is selected and only its reward is observed.

Bernoulli bandit rewards. The lower-bound witness uses independent Bernoulli draws conditional on its fixed mean path, independent of the policy seed. Independence is an explicit hard-subclass construction, not an added restriction on the policy class.

The horizon uncertainty set is exactly L(V_T). Section 2 additionally describes a nondecreasing budget sequence with V_1=0, KV_t<=t and V_2=2/K; Theorem 1 separately states the horizon range [1/K,T/K]. The local argument establishes that full horizon range without requiring an extension to such a sequence.
statement.conclusion: For every pi in P, R^pi(V_T,T)>=c(KV_T)^(1/3)T^(2/3), hence R^*(V_T,T)>=c(KV_T)^(1/3)T^(2/3). The local repair supplies c=1/(32sqrt(2)); this is not the source's final printed coefficient.
statement.objects_and_definitions: K arms and horizon T. V(mu;T)=sum_{t=1}^{T-1} max_k |mu_{t+1}^k-mu_t^k|; L(V_T)={mu in [0,1]^(K x T):V(mu;T)<=V_T}. P consists of all measurable nonanticipating policies using their independent random seed and past selected-arm rewards. R^pi(mu,T)=sum_t max_k mu_t^k-E^pi sum_t mu_t^{I_t}; R^pi(V_T,T)=sup_{mu in L(V_T)}R^pi(mu,T); R^*(V_T,T)=inf_{pi in P}R^pi(V_T,T).
statement.parameter_domains: Integer K>=2, integer T>=2, real V_T in [1/K,T/K]. Natural logarithms in the local argument.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There is a universal c>0, uniform in K,T,V_T: for every displayed parameter choice and every pi in P there exists an oblivious deterministic admissible mean path, with the specified Bernoulli oracle, such that expected dynamic pseudoregret is at least c(KV_T)^(1/3)T^(2/3). Expectation includes reward draws and all policy randomization. The finite prior is a proof device, not an adaptive adversary.

content.version_comparison: P100 p.1 visibly identifies arXiv:1405.3316v2 [cs.LG], 6 Jun 2019, Besbes/Gur/Zeevi, with manuscript date April 4, 2019. This matches published src.P100 revision 1 and its original PDF SHA256; its version, identity and scope are preserved. The additional Auer SIAM 2002 paper has different authors, title, model and statements. Its Appendix A initially fixes a deterministic policy via an oblivious-adversary seed argument and independent Bernoulli construction; P100 requires fresh batches and conditioning on the actual prior history. The local argument supplies that transfer explicitly. Auer's KL definition uses base-2 lg, but Lemma A.1's final bound uses natural ln; the local derivation uses natural logs throughout. Corollary 3.2 is a fixed-reward-array best-static-action bound, not by itself the missing full-range P100 upper-bound proof.
